statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday settle and do not reopen inside this horizon, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists in any published hour and Tail is held at a closed-venue floor. Stress stays in the upper elevated band because the US-Iran tanker exchange in the Strait of Hormuz is two-sided and unresolved, with the Iranian counter-claim still unconfirmed by CENTCOM.
recommendation: Tail holds a 4-7% closed-venue floor across all 24 published hours, so the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green throughout. Stress opens at 56%, eases to 53% through the dormant Sunday overnight window and rebuilds to a 66% peak as the horizon tracks toward the 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen, crossing into the high band only in the final two slots. Confidence declines from 86% to 77% as later slots rest on progressively older evidence. No danger window is published, because a closed venue cannot produce the price path the Tail score is defined on.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 through the CME weekend halt as the Hormuz tanker exchange stays two-sided and unconfirmed, with crude holding a near-10% weekly gain and VIX still under 15
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions inside that session, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday settle and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on 6 September, two hours after the final slot of this forecast, so the last print remains the only anchor and no published hour can contain observable price action.

The geopolitical sequence is unchanged from the previous assessment and one hour older. US Central Command says American forces struck three Iranian crude oil tankers on Saturday after an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer evaded ballistic missiles fired by the IRGC Navy; the M/T Downy near Kharg Island and the M/T Stark 1 near Jask were permanently disabled and the M/T Kylo was destroyed in the Gulf of Oman. Adm. Brad Cooper framed the action as a tanker-for-tanker economic cost. The IRGC subsequently claimed it had targeted three oil tankers and three US-affiliated ships in the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation, and warned shipping against unauthorised transit. CENTCOM has not confirmed that Iranian counter-claim, and no verified follow-on step has been reported in the intervening hour. The campaign is therefore two-sided and unresolved rather than escalating, which is why Stress carries it and Tail does not.

Cross-asset context remains conflicted rather than aligned, which under the published definitions raises Stress and lowers conviction without amplifying Tail. WTI trades at $91.48 after a weekly gain of about 9%, its strongest week since mid-July, with Brent at $96.28. Yet equity volatility has barely transmitted any of it: VIX closed Friday at 14.53, up 1.47% on the day and still under 15. Rates are the second unresolved input, with the 2-year at 4.34% and the 10-year at 4.77% on the latest H.15 release after the August payroll surprise pushed September pricing hawkish, and with public pressure on the Fed, including a threat to halt trade with deficit countries unless rates are cut, adding noise rather than information. Delayed latest-session futures context is consistent with that split rather than with a one-way tape.

None of this can be expressed in price until the venue reopens. Tail therefore stays at a closed-venue floor of 5%, easing to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and widening to 7% only as the horizon approaches the venue timeline, which keeps every published hour mapped to EA_ON and green. Stress carries the escalation instead, opening at 56% and building to 66% in the final slots where the largest volume of unpriced weekend information meets the shortest remaining interval to a live quote. The US Monday macro calendar is empty, so the first scheduled checkpoint after the reopen is Tuesday's NFIB release, ahead of PPI and jobless claims on Thursday and CPI on Friday.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span the Friday 21:00 UTC futures settlement and the first twenty-three hours of the CME weekend halt. Every one of the 24 slots is available from published Claude assessments, every one is scored at the closed-venue Tail floor of 5% under a normal mode, and every one maps to EA_ON and green. Stress was flat at 38% from the settlement through 10:00 UTC on 5 September, then climbed steadily from 39% at 11:00 UTC to 42% by 14:00 UTC as the Saturday US-Iran sequence developed, stepped to 48% at 15:00 UTC once the CENTCOM tanker strikes were verified, and rose again to 52% by 19:00 UTC and 57% at 20:00 UTC when the Iranian counter-claim was published. Confidence held in a narrow 85-88% band throughout, reflecting a complete evidence set in which only the live price path is unavailable.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, which does not end until 22:00 UTC on 6 September, two hours after the final published slot, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-7% closed-venue floor, easing through the dormant middle of the weekend and widening only as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline; that widening is a gap allowance, not evidence of directional structure. Stress opens at 56%, eases to a 53% low in the quietest overnight hours, ticks up as Tel Aviv and Gulf venues open on Sunday morning and provide the first non-US quote since Friday, then rebuilds to a 66% peak into Sunday evening, crossing from the elevated into the high band in the final two slots. The drivers are a two-sided and unconfirmed Hormuz tanker campaign, a near-10% weekly crude gain and hawkish September rate pricing, none of which has met an equity quote since Friday. Confidence declines from 86% to 77% because later slots rest on progressively older evidence during an actively developing sequence. The reopening auction is the first hour in which structure can be scored: orderly two-way retracement would decay both scores quickly, while repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the first genuine Tail amplifier.
